text:
liz_support: forwarding a customer ticket — ACME is seeing intermittent 400s on the embeddings endpoint and big tail latency spikes. They say error says `dimension mismatch` but only for a subset of requests, looks correlated with bursts. Ticket: https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/ACME-987

liz_support: repro notes from customer: they call `POST /v1/embeddings` with model `redwood-embed-768-v1`, some requests are single-item, others batched by client (variable sizes). They recently toggled `dynamic_batching=true` and lowered `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 16 to reduce latency. Spike started after that change.

liz_support: pasted example payload they sent (sanitized):
```json
{"model":"redwood-embed-768-v1","input":["How to fix batch spikes?","Short query"]}
```

liz_support: error from platform they pasted: `400 Bad Request: embedding dimension mismatch (expected 768, got 1024)`. They say ~0.3% of calls fail, but during bursts it goes up to ~8% and overall latency p95 jumps from 180ms -> 1.2s.

devon_infra: thanks — quick Qs: 1) are they using any SDK that might auto-pad or attach variant tags? 2) do they route to multiple model aliases? 3) can we get a sample failing request+headers (esp `x-client-model` / `x-variant` if present)?

liz_support: answered — they use internal SDK that does some client-side batching, not adding model tags. They call different model names in prod for A/B (ex: `redwood-embed-768-v1` and `redwood-embed-768-v1-quant`). They say client batches sometimes mix responses from two upstream calls into one batch (our suspicion). Attached sanitized headers: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>`, `X-Client-Batch-Id: batch-2026-03-15-19`, no variant header.

jima_engineer: wondering if dynamic coalescing could be merging requests across model variants when names are close — we have guard rails but there was a recent change to make coalescing key looser to improve throughput. ops-bot: deploy-log for coalescer: rollout 2026-03-14 03:12 UTC, change-id `coalesce-loosen-0b9a`.

natalie_sre: tagging perf — that rollout saw a 6% throughput gain on embeddings in canary but also added a path that uses `model_family` instead of full model id for coalescing. Could explain cross-variant merges if model ids are aliased.

devon_infra: ask customer to repro with `dynamic_batching=false` and `max_batch_size=64` (their old config). Also request a HAR/log of a failing call with base64 body if possible. If failures stop, points to coalescing.

liz_support: they tried toggling `dynamic_batching=false` and failures dropped to 0.05% and p95 back to ~210ms. They can run more tests tomorrow — asked for a temporary mitigation we can flip server-side while we investigate.

jima_engineer: preliminary root cause hypothesis: coalescer key used `model_family` for merging after change-id `coalesce-loosen-0b9a`. Some customers use variant suffixes that change quantization/dims (e.g., `-quant`), so coalescing mixed requests with differing expected embed dims. When we pack the batch, we don't re-check per-item dims after merge (bug). That would explain intermittent dim errors and spikes during bursts.

devon_infra: can we confirm by searching logs for `coalesce-loosen` timeframe and errors with `expected 768 got 1024` and matching `coalesced_batch_id`? I'll run a query in datadog.

ops-bot: query job submitted: logs.search("expected 768 got 1024 AND coalesced_batch_id:*") -> 123 matches between 2026-03-14 and 2026-03-16. Top hit shows `coalesced_batch_id=batch-zz-9012` and `models: [redwood-embed-768-v1, redwood-embed-768-v1-quant]`.

natalie_sre: OK that confirms mixing. Severity: customer impact small but rising during bursts. Recommend rollback of change-id `coalesce-loosen-0b9a` or patch to include full model id in coalesce key.

jima_engineer: pushing a hotfix to check per-request `expected_dim` before final pack + reject incompatible joins. Draft PR `coalesce:check-dim-before-pack` -> diff link: https://git.internal/r/34567. Will canary to 5% then 50%.

devon_infra: also patch telemetry to emit `coalesce_reason` and include model id list in logs so support can triage faster.

liz_support: customer asked if we can flip a server-side toggle now — can we temporarily force coalescing to use full model id for their org?

jima_engineer: yes, we have an org-scoped coalesce policy flag. I'll flip for ACME account: `coalesce_key=full_model_id` and confirm.

ops-bot: config change applied for org `acme-corp` by jima_engineer at 2026-03-15T19:21:12Z.

liz_support: confirmed with customer — failures dropped immediately and p95 improved in minutes. Customer very relieved.

devon_infra: next actions: 1) ship hotfix and canary, 2) add telemetry & an alert for mixed-model coalescing errors, 3) reach out to customers who use variant suffixes to recommend not loosening coalesce key.

natalie_sre: I'll open a postmortem note and link to the PR + rollout plan. tagging @eng-leads.

liz_support: thanks everyone — I'll update the ACME ticket with timeline, mitigation steps, and invite them to a postmortem call next week. :thumbsup:

jima_engineer: FYI hotfix PR merged to main, canary deploy started 2026-03-15T20:45Z. commit `a1f3d2c`.

ops-bot: canary results after 30m: error rate for `expected_dim_mismatch` down 98% on canary nodes.

devon_infra: leaving this thread open until full rollout. good catch — this one would've been noisy in peak.

liz_support: noted, closing once rollout done and postmortem published. Thanks all.
